rationale: The student added 30 + 20 = 50 and 7 + 6 = 13 and concatenated them to form 513 rather than regrouping 10 ones into 1 ten. Demonstrating 'make-a-ten' shows how a pile of ones greater than 9 bundles into 1 ten and leftover ones.
intent: Demonstrate make-a-ten on the place-value with values [14]. Tutor points at: 10 ones regrouping into 1 ten

frames.caption: Here are 14 ones. That is too many for the ones place: it can only hold 0 to 9.
Bundle ten of them. Ten ones make one ten, so the bundle moves to the tens place. 4 ones are left.
Write 1 in the tens place and 4 in the ones place: 14. One digit per place.

judgement.reasoning: The student writes both digits of the ones sum in the ones column (e.g., writing 513 for 37 + 26). This short demo explicitly demonstrates that a place value column can only hold 0 to 9, showing 14 ones bundling into 1 ten and 4 ones, directly addressing why and how 13 ones must be split.
judgement.verdict: A teacher would definitely use this clear demonstration because it directly targets the single-digit place-value constraint the student is violating.
